title: Expensya Homepage Teardown: Oct 2020 to Jun 2026
h1: How Expensya rewrote its homepage over 6 years
metaTitle: Expensya Homepage CRO Teardown — Oct 2020 to Jun 2026
description: A CRO teardown of Expensya's homepage from Oct 2020 to Jun 2026 — what changed in headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation, and what SaaS teams can study from it.
excerpt: Expensya's homepage didn't just get updated. The headline, section headings, CTAs, navigation all shifted in a consistent direction between Oct 2020 and Jun 2026. This teardown maps what changed, when, and what the patterns may suggest.
author: Wael Aouididi
authorBio: SaaS Growth Marketer and fractional growth lead. I help B2B SaaS founders diagnose landing page, CRO, positioning, and analytics leaks before scaling traffic.

analysisBlocks.label: Oct 2020 — original state
analysisBlocks.heading: The original: product-led messaging
annotations: H1 opens with: "Automated spend management for all companies" — direct product statement.

Visible section headings include: "Equip yourself with the most comprehensive business spend and expense management solution, tailored to your needs and to those of your teams", "Expensya fully automates your business expenditure", "A solution designed for every company".

Section headings later removed include: "Equip yourself with the most comprehensive business spend and expense management solution, tailored to your needs and to those of your teams" and "Expensya fully automates your business expenditure".

analysisBlocks.label: Jun 2026 — current state
analysisBlocks.heading: Today: updated positioning
annotations: H1 now reads: "Voici à quoi devrait ressembler la gestion des dépenses." — updated value proposition.
New section headings include: "Améliorez la conformité. Réduisez les risques. Obtenez une visibilité complète sur les dépenses.", "Cartes de paiement & budgets", "Politiques de dépenses".
CTAs no longer present include: "Free trial", "Discover our solutions", "Find out more".

lessonCards.title: Your H1 signals which buyer you are targeting
lessonCards.body: The headline changed from "Automated spend management for all companies" to "Voici à quoi devrait ressembler la gestion des dépenses.". The framing of your H1 is one of the clearest signals of which buyer you are targeting and what you expect them to do next.

lessonCards.title: Navigation is a positioning statement
lessonCards.body: Navigation items changed from "Small", "Mid", "Large" to "En savoir plus", "Se connecter", "Contacter un commercial". The labels your navigation uses reveal what you think your visitor is trying to decide — and who that visitor is.

lessonCards.title: Section headings reveal what the team thinks buyers care about
lessonCards.body: 14 section headings were added and 7 removed between Oct 2020 and Jun 2026. New headings include "Améliorez la conformité. Réduisez les risques. Obtenez une visibilité complète sur les dépenses." and "Cartes de paiement & budgets". Headings that disappeared include "Equip yourself with the most comprehensive business spend and expense management solution, tailored to your needs and to those of your teams" and "Expensya fully automates your business expenditure". The pattern of what gets added and removed is one of the clearest signals of how a team is re-prioritizing its value proposition.

lessonCards.title: Incremental changes compound into a brand shift
lessonCards.body: Across 2 snapshots spanning roughly 6 years, no single update here was a dramatic overhaul. The end state looks very different from the start because small, consistent changes in the same direction accumulate. This is worth studying if your own homepage has been drifting without a clear direction.
